criteria.tailor: The control applies, but the organization sets its own value, scope or wording.
criteria.exclude: The control cannot apply to any in-scope project. The reason is recorded.

vocabulary.meaning: A solution going through design assessment. It has one record in CRISP.
One testable security statement adopted by cyber leadership. It has an owner, a source and an evidence definition.
A rule that says which requirements apply to a project, and why.
A fact about a project that rules use, such as data class or exposure.
The proof that shows a requirement is met, such as a design detail, a passed test or a confirmed control.
The evidence defined for the requirement is present and complete.
Some of the defined evidence is present, but not all of it.
The requirement applies and the design does not show it is met.
A gap that a person with authority outside CRISP has accepted. The decision reference is recorded in CRISP.
The requirement applies but nobody has judged it yet.
Reachable from outside the organization's network, with or without sign-in.
A pre-approved design that already meets a known set of requirements.
The security level a project of a given category must reach, with a way to measure it.
Security design assessment. The preliminary SDA is produced in Phase 1, updated in Phase 2 and finalized in Phase 3.

requirements.title: Account management
requirements.statement: User and service accounts are created, reviewed and removed through a defined process with a named owner.

evidence.addressed: The design names the account lifecycle process, the account owner, and the review frequency.
evidence.partly_addressed: An account process exists but the owner or review frequency is not defined.

requirements.title: Least privilege
requirements.statement: Each user, service and component has only the access it needs to do its job.

evidence.addressed: The design lists roles and the permissions of each, and shows administrator rights are separate from normal rights.
evidence.partly_addressed: Roles are defined but some components use shared or broad permissions.

requirements.title: Authentication
requirements.statement: Every user is uniquely identified and authenticated before access to the project is allowed.

evidence.addressed: The design shows sign-in through the organization's approved identity provider for all users.
evidence.partly_addressed: Sign-in uses the approved provider for some users or paths only.

requirements.title: Multi-factor authentication
requirements.statement: Multi-factor authentication is required for administrator access and for any user access from outside the organization's network.

evidence.addressed: Design or configuration shows multi-factor authentication enforced on every administrator and external sign-in path, with no bypass.
evidence.partly_addressed: Multi-factor authentication is enforced on some sign-in paths, or for administrators only.
accepted_evidence: Test showing sign-in without a second factor is refused

requirements.title: Secrets and credentials
requirements.statement: Passwords, keys and tokens used by the solution are kept in an approved secrets store and never in code or configuration files.

evidence.addressed: The design names the secrets store, and a code scan shows no secrets in the repository.
evidence.partly_addressed: A secrets store is named but the scan was not run or found exceptions.

requirements.title: Encryption at rest
requirements.statement: Confidential and restricted data is encrypted wherever it is stored.

evidence.addressed: The design lists every data store holding this data and shows each is encrypted with an approved algorithm.
evidence.partly_addressed: Some data stores are encrypted and others are not, or a store is missing from the list.

requirements.title: Encryption in transit
requirements.statement: Data is protected with approved encryption whenever it moves between components or leaves the internal network.

evidence.addressed: The data flow diagram shows an approved protocol on every connection.
evidence.partly_addressed: Some connections use unencrypted protocols, or are not shown in the diagram.

requirements.title: Key management
requirements.statement: Encryption keys are created, stored, rotated and retired using an approved key management service.

evidence.addressed: The design names the key service, the rotation period and who can access keys.
evidence.partly_addressed: A key service is named but rotation or access is not defined.

requirements.title: Session protection
requirements.statement: User sessions are protected against theft and reuse, and end after a defined idle time.

evidence.addressed: The design defines token lifetime, secure cookie settings, idle timeout and logout behavior.
evidence.partly_addressed: Some of these settings are defined but not all.

requirements.title: Security event logging
requirements.statement: Security-relevant events are logged with who, what, when and where, and sent to the central logging platform.

evidence.addressed: The design lists the events logged, the fields in each entry, and shows delivery to the central platform.
evidence.partly_addressed: Logging exists but events, fields or central delivery are incomplete.

requirements.title: Log review
requirements.statement: Security logs are reviewed on a defined schedule, and suspicious activity is followed up.

evidence.addressed: Alerts and a review schedule are defined, and an owner is named.
evidence.partly_addressed: A review is planned but the schedule or owner is missing.

requirements.title: Backup and restore
requirements.statement: Data and configuration are backed up at a frequency set by criticality, and restoring from backup is tested.

evidence.addressed: Backup frequency, retention and a successful restore test are documented.
evidence.partly_addressed: Backups are defined but no restore test has been done.

requirements.title: Vulnerability scanning
requirements.statement: The solution and its platform are scanned for known vulnerabilities at least monthly, and findings are fixed within agreed time frames.

evidence.addressed: The project is enrolled in scanning and a recent scan result is available.
evidence.partly_addressed: The project is enrolled but the scan result is old or findings are unresolved.

requirements.title: Boundary protection
requirements.statement: Traffic into and out of the project passes through approved controls, and only the needed connections are allowed.

evidence.addressed: The design shows all inbound and outbound traffic passing through approved controls, with an allowed connection list.
evidence.partly_addressed: Approved controls exist but some paths bypass them.

requirements.title: Input validation
requirements.statement: All input from users and other systems is checked before it is used.

evidence.addressed: The design describes validation for every input path, and a test shows invalid input is refused.
evidence.partly_addressed: Validation is described for some inputs only, or no test was run.
accepted_evidence: Design document section on input handling

requirements.title: Security testing
requirements.statement: The solution is security tested before release, and findings are fixed or formally accepted.

evidence.addressed: A security test plan exists, and results show no unresolved critical or high findings.
evidence.partly_addressed: A test plan exists but testing is not complete, or findings are unresolved.

requirements.title: Third-party components
requirements.statement: Third-party software components are listed and checked for known vulnerabilities and untrusted sources.

evidence.addressed: A component list exists and a recent check shows no unresolved critical findings.
evidence.partly_addressed: A component list exists but no vulnerability check has been done.

patterns.limits: Does not cover mobile apps or file upload features.

Sign-in uses the central identity provider with multi-factor authentication (check the identity provider policy).

patterns.fits_when: project_type is api and exposure is internal
patterns.limits: Does not cover APIs shared with partners.
measurement: All calls pass the internal gateway (check the network diagram).
Each caller has its own credential (check the credential list).

threat_library.threat: An attacker pretends to be a legitimate user or administrator.
A session token or cookie is stolen and reused.
Crafted input changes how the application behaves.
A user denies an action and nobody can prove otherwise.
Data is read directly from a data store.
Data is intercepted while moving between components.
Backup copies are stolen or exposed.
A password, key or token is exposed in code or configuration.
Traffic floods or exhausts the service.
A user or component uses permissions it should not have.
A third-party component contains a flaw or malicious code.

threat_checklist.check: A data flow diagram exists and lists all components and data stores.
Every data flow and every component has at least one threat considered, or a recorded reason none applies.
Every threat is linked to at least one planned control or recorded as a gap.
Every threat in the model exists in the threat library, or is flagged as new for the cyber team to review.
The architect has reviewed the model and signed it off.

risk_methodology.purpose: One approved way to rate risk, so priority and posture are consistent and can be defended.

impact.scale: 1 to 4, taken from the attribute scores

likelihood.scale: 1 to 4, taken from the attribute scores

residual_risk.formula: inherent score x status factor, rounded to the nearest whole number, minimum 1
residual_risk.risk_accepted: The status factor of the underlying status still applies. Acceptance is recorded with its decision reference, conditions and expiry date. It does not change the rating.

overrides.limit: Up or down by one rating level.
overrides.record: Original rating, new rating, reason, approver, date.

fields: Evidence for the change (for example override or false-match records)

versioning.patch: Wording fixes that do not change meaning.
versioning.minor: A new or changed requirement, rule, pattern, target or threat library entry.
versioning.major: A change in framework basis or in the risk methodology calculation.
versioning.pinning: A project stays on the catalog version it started with. A move needs the security architect's request and the cyber team's agreement. The reason is recorded.

approvals.change: New or changed requirement, rule, pattern, target or threat library entry (minor)
Framework adopt, tailor or exclude decision

approvals.approver: Governance board, with cyber risk (methodology owner)

approvals.change: Change in framework basis or risk calculation (major)

release_steps: Change is proposed as a pull request.
Reviewers approve. Required approvers depend on the table above.
Cyber team tags the release and builds the catalog bundle.
Pilot or new projects are pinned to the new version. Existing projects stay where they are.
